title: Austin's Air, Land, & Convention Center Future
summary:
*   City leaders received an update on Austin's critical air quality program.
*   Discussions focused on the land management plan for the Balcones Canyonland Preserves, a key ecological area.
*   Officials reviewed the financial health and future outlook of the Austin Convention Center.
transcript:
Austin City Council
MINUTES
WORKSESSION
WEDNESDAY, MARCH 6, 2002
The following represents the actions taken by the Austin City Council in the order they
occurred during the meeting. While the minutes are not in sequential order, all agenda
items were discussed.
The City Council of Austin, Texas convened in a Work Session on Wednesday, March 6,
2002 at One Texas Center, 505 Barton Springs Road, third floor training room, Austin,
Texas.
Mayor Garcia called the meeting to order at 10:06 a.m.
BRIEFINGS
1. 
City of Austin Air Quality Program Update
The presentation was made by Lisa Gordon, Assistant City Manger; Austan
Librach, Director; and Fred Blood, Manager, Transportation, Planning and
Sustainability
2. 
Balcones Canyonland Preserves Land Management Plan
The presentation was made by Roger Chan, Assistant City Manager; Chris Lippe,
Director, Water and Wastewater Department; Michael Heitz, Director, Watershed
Protection; Junie Plummer, Property Agent, Public Works Department; and Willie
Conrad, Manager, Environmental Conservation Program.
3. 
Convention Center Fiscal Update
The presentation was made by Roger Chan, Assistant City Manager; John
Stephens, Director, Financial Services; Bob Hodges, Director; Larry Anderson,
Chief Financial Officer, Convention Center; and Bob Lander, President, Austin
Convention and Visitors' Bureau
The motion to adjourn the meeting at 12:13 p.m. was approved on Council Member
Griffith's motion, Council Member Slusher's second by a 7-0 vote.
The amended minutes from the regular meeting of February 14, 2002 and the minutes from
the Work Session of March 6, 2002 and the regular meeting from March 7, 2002 were
approved on Council Member Thomas' motion, Council Member Wynn's second by a 7-0
vote.
